text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Elevated 5xx and connection timeouts observed for customer Greenline on reserved-pool cluster rpool-phi7. Error rate >10%% above baseline for the last 3m. Linked runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/gpu-pressure

priya-oncall: I'm paged, reading in. Confirming impact window and whether traffic was recently shifted?

sam-kim: I see the spike in the dashboard — p50 latency ok but p99 token latency shoots and 500s on gateway. Repro: small batch requests cause worker OOMs.

maya-ops: Logs from the worker hosts show repeated eviction messages and CUDA OOMs. Possible noisy-neighbor or sudden batch-size change.

priya-oncall: tagging ops-bot for host-level metrics and Lex for any recent model changes @lex-devex

ops-bot: Host summary for rpool-phi7 (last 5m):
```
- GPU utilization: host-03 98%%, host-04 96%%, host-07 87%%
- GPU memory used: host-03 24GB/24GB, host-04 23.8GB/24GB
- Kernel restarts: host-03 4
- Processes spiking: pid 4210 (customer=greenline) and pid 6122 (customer=atlas)
```

elaine-custeng: I'm on the customer call with Greenline, they report intermittent 500s and model truncation. They're seeing increased latency and some requests erroring out.

priya-oncall: Ok. Sam, can you run a diagnostic on the model workers to confirm whether it's application-level OOM vs GPU memory pressure?

sam-kim: Running diag command and grabbing tail of worker logs now:
```
$ rpoolctl exec --host host-03 sudo journalctl -u redwood-worker -n 200
[...]
E tensorflow: Ran out of GPU memory allocating 512MB
E redwood.worker: eviction triggered for model_id=red-2024-l1
```

sam-kim: Definitely GPU memory exhaustion on host-03. Host-04 similar. Host-07 less but catching up.

maya-ops: Looking at per-tenant usage, atlas has a huge burst of concurrent long-context runs right around the same time. They are on a different tenant but same reserved pool.

priya-oncall: That matches noisy-neighbor. Immediate mitigations: 1) throttle Greenline concurrency, 2) migrate Greenline to another node if capacity exists, 3) evict/limit Atlas burst or enable temporary burst limits. Which is fastest?

maya-ops: Fastest is to move Greenline off the saturated hosts to host-07,08 if they have room. But host-07 has some headroom. Migration takes ~30s per worker. We can also enable per-tenant GPU mem quota (soft limit) to prevent future noisy bursts.

lex-devex: I can flip the routing rule to prefer hosts 07/08 for Greenline and reduce concurrency to 2 for their route. Will need approval.

priya-oncall: Approving temporary routing change + concurrency cap. Also open PR for quota enforcement after incident.

sam-kim: Applying routing change:
```
$ rctl route update --customer greenline --prefer-host host-07,host-08 --concurrency 2
OK: routing updated, rebalancing 6 workers
```

ops-bot: Rebalance progress: 2/6 workers migrated, 5s per worker. Host-03 GPU memory now at 86%% after stop of some processes.

maya-ops: Rebalance done. Host-03 GPU mem down to 62%%, host-07 usage up to 78%%. 5xx rate dropping.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigation in progress. Current 5xx rate down from 12%% to 3%% over baseline. Continue monitoring for 15m to validate.

elaine-custeng: Told Greenline we've applied a routing change and temporary concurrency cap. They asked if this will affect throughput — yes slight throughput reduction but fewer errors. They requested ETA for full fix.

priya-oncall: Next steps: 1) make per-tenant GPU soft-quota permanent, 2) add alert for sudden per-tenant GPU mem delta, 3) follow-up with Atlas team to schedule a longer-term quota or rate-limit for their bursty job.

sam-kim: Filing ticket INF-4321 for per-tenant quota with proposed limits and rollout plan.

lex-devex: Also adding a console note explaining routing fallback and how to pin tenants to nodes for safety.

maya-ops: Quick postmortem notes: root cause = concurrent long-context runs from Atlas led to GPU mem saturation on two hosts in the reserved pool; lack of per-tenant mem quotas allowed noisy neighbor effect; migration and concurrency cap reduced errors.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation successful. 5xx rate back to normal for 10m window. Recommend: follow runbook actions A/B/C and schedule post-incident review.

customer-eng: Greenline confirmed errors went away and are monitoring. They want a summary and a timeline for quota implementation — I'll prepare customer-facing note.

priya-oncall: Thanks all. I'll run the incident bridge notes and assign follow-ups: INF-4321 (quota), OPS-4322 (alerting), COMMS-4323 (customer note). Handoff to day SRE: @maya-ops for monitoring.

maya-ops: Acknowledged handoff, will monitor next 4 hours.

sam-kim: Pushed quick fix PR to backend to surface per-tenant mem usage in console: PR #789.

lex-devex: I'll add a short doc snippet to the runbook about route-prefers and emergency migrations.

incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated). Final metrics snapshot: peak 5xx 13%% -> now 0.8%%, mean p99 latency improved by 110ms. Bridge closed at ts 1855557832.

priya-oncall: Closing thread, will link postmortem when ready. Thanks team.
